title: Converge deferred weight loader and streaming activation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The current model ingest pipeline mixes eager weight deserialization with tokenizer initialization and synchronous shard activation. This causes high peak CPU/GPU memory during cold starts, poor tail latency for large models, and brittle ordering assumptions between tokenizer and KV-cache warmup.

Goal: Refactor the loader into a converged, small-surface "deferred weight loader" that supports streaming shard activation, idempotent tokenizer warmstart, and integrity-checked manifests. Deliver measurable reductions in cold-start memory and 95th/99th latency for first-request path while keeping compatibility with existing checkpoint formats.

Approach:
- Introduce a single Loader facade that exposes: manifest validation, async shard fetch (HTTP/S3), staged deserialization (metadata -> weights -> device upload), and a streaming activate() API that binds shards to runtime without blocking request threads.
- Decouple tokenizer warmstart from weight deserialization: tokenizer init runs from manifest metadata and a cached token table; full tokenizer asset fetch is async and retries independently.
- Add atomic shard state machine (PENDING -> LOADING -> READY -> FAILED) persisted in in-memory manifest to support retries and concurrent activations.
- Replace ad-hoc pickle-based auxiliary assets with protobuf v4 schema for manifests and tokenizer-lite blobs (upgrade dependency).
- Ensure backwards compatibility by shipshimming old manifest fields and provide a migration path that auto-detects legacy manifests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cold-start peak GPU memory reduced by >= 15% in benchmark harness for base-13B model.
- First-request 95th latency improved by >= 20% in synthetic load.
- No regressions in streaming generation throughput (±5%).
- Unit and e2e tests cover manifest parsing, shard state transitions, tokenizer warmstart, and failure/retry behavior.
- Migration path documented and flag-gated for controlled rollout.

Migration & Rollout:
- Feature flag (loader.v2) off by default. Canary enable for dedicated infra, then staged by model catalog and customer opt-in.
- Provide an admin tool to reconcile manifest states and force-shard reactivation.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Tokenizer mismatch during async warmstart causing subtle tokenization errors. Mitigation: strict manifest hash checks and a conservative fallback that forces synchronous tokenizer init for models with recorded tokenization deltas.
- Risk: New protobuf dependency surfaces incompatibilities. Mitigation: pin v4.* and include a compatibility shim that falls back to legacy parsing on parse errors.
comments: 2025-11-04 - Triage: flagged as P1 tech-debt after benchmarking spike in Nov infra run. Assigned to Diego.
2025-11-07 - Design review: decided on single Loader facade and state machine. Trade-off: slightly larger surface area but simpler runtime contract. Reviewed by Lina Gupta, Ben Horowitz.
2025-11-10 - Prototype: implemented async shard fetch + staged deserialization in branch feat/loader-v2. Initial microbench shows -12% peak memory on 13B local harness (needs cluster run).
2025-11-13 - CI: added unit tests for shard state transitions and manifest parsing. Found race condition in concurrent activate() (fixed with per-shard mutex and idempotency token).

2025-11-16 - Integration: ran canary on dedicated pool (3 nodes). Results: 18% cold-start peak memory reduction, 22% improvement in 95th first-request latency. Noted 2% throughput variance under sustained 1000qps — investigating batching interaction.

2025-11-18 - PR: opened github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248 implementing loader, protobuf manifest, and tokenizer warmstart shim. Reviewers: @lgupta, @mroberts. Blocking item: documentation for admin reconcile tool.
Next steps: finish docs, add e2e SKU tests, coordinate with runtime-1.21 release window, and schedule a canary rollout plan for 2025-11-26.
